hints: A minimum set of roads whose removal disconnects 1 from n has size equal to the maximum number of edge-disjoint 1-to-n routes.
Model each road as capacity 1 and compute maximum flow.
After max flow, the residual reachable set identifies the roads crossing the minimum cut.
analogy: Find how many independent routes can carry traffic; those many roads form a smallest cut separating the endpoints.
example: If two edge-disjoint routes connect 1 to n, at least two roads must be removed to block every route.
algorithm: Build unit-capacity edges, run max-flow, then BFS the residual graph from 1. Output each original road from reachable to unreachable endpoints.
correctness: Max-flow/min-cut gives equality between the maximum edge-disjoint route count and minimum cut capacity; the residual boundary is such a minimum cut.
complexity: O(V^2 E) time using Edmonds-Karp; O(V+E) memory.
